    Model Selection: BIC, AIC, and ICL¶

    This notebook demonstrates tgmm.select_model, the Phase 1 (v0.4 roadmap) model-selection sweep, and GaussianMixture.icl, the Integrated Completed Likelihood (Biernacki, Celeux & Govaert, 2000).

    BIC and AIC score a fitted mixture purely on log-likelihood plus a complexity penalty -- they don't care whether the mixture's components are cleanly separated or heavily overlapping, as long as the extra components earn their keep in likelihood. ICL adds an entropy penalty for ambiguous assignments (-2 * sum_i log(responsibility of the point's most likely component)), so on data with overlapping clusters it tends to prefer fewer, better-separated components than BIC does on the same data, even though both reduce to the same thing when clusters are perfectly separated (one-hot responsibilities).

    In [1]:
    Copied! 
    import numpy as np
import torch
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import os

os.chdir('../')

from tgmm import GaussianMixture, generate_gmm_data, select_model
from tgmm.plotting import CATEGORICAL_PALETTE

random_state = 42
np.random.seed(random_state)
torch.manual_seed(random_state)

    A dataset with overlapping blobs¶

    Five true components in two dimensions: two pairs that overlap substantially ((0, 0)/(2.2, 0) and (6, 6)/(8.2, 6)), plus one isolated component ((0, 2.2)). Each pair is close enough relative to its spread that a 2- or 3-component mixture can already explain most of the likelihood in that region -- the point of this dataset is to make BIC and ICL disagree about how many of the five "true" components are worth resolving separately.

    In [2]:
    Copied! 
    centers = [
    np.array([0.0, 0.0]),
    np.array([2.2, 0.0]),
    np.array([0.0, 2.2]),
    np.array([6.0, 6.0]),
    np.array([8.2, 6.0]),
]
covs = [np.eye(2) for _ in centers]
n_samples = [150] * len(centers)

X, true_labels = generate_gmm_data(centers, covs, n_samples, random_state=random_state)

plt.figure(figsize=(5, 5))
for k in range(len(centers)):
    mask = true_labels == k
    plt.scatter(X[mask, 0], X[mask, 1], s=10, color=CATEGORICAL_PALETTE[k % len(CATEGORICAL_PALETTE)],
                label=f'true component {k}')
plt.legend(fontsize=8)
plt.title('Overlapping blobs (true generating components)')
plt.gca().set_aspect('equal')
plt.show()

    Sweep n_components with select_model¶

    select_model fits a GaussianMixture for every requested n_components, recording bic, aic, icl, the final log-likelihood, and whether each fit converged.

    In [3]:
    Copied! 
    result = select_model(
    X,
    n_components=range(1, 9),
    covariance_types=('full',),
    criterion='bic',
    n_init=3,
    random_state=0,
    max_iter=200,
)

for row in result.table:
    print(f"K={row['n_components']}  bic={row['bic']:.1f}  aic={row['aic']:.1f}  "
          f"icl={row['icl']:.1f}  icl-bic={row['icl'] - row['bic']:.1f}  converged={row['converged']}")
    result = select_model( X, n_components=range(1, 9), covariance_types=('full',), criterion='bic', n_init=3, random_state=0, max_iter=200, ) for row in result.table: print(f"K={row['n_components']} bic={row['bic']:.1f} aic={row['aic']:.1f} " f"icl={row['icl']:.1f} icl-bic={row['icl'] - row['bic']:.1f} converged={row['converged']}")

    BIC vs. ICL curves¶

    Both criteria are "lower is better." Watch where each curve's minimum sits.

    In [4]:
    Copied! 
    ks = [row['n_components'] for row in result.table]
bics = [row['bic'] for row in result.table]
icls = [row['icl'] for row in result.table]

best_bic_k = ks[int(np.argmin(bics))]
best_icl_k = ks[int(np.argmin(icls))]

plt.figure(figsize=(6, 4))
plt.plot(ks, bics, marker='o', label='BIC')
plt.plot(ks, icls, marker='s', label='ICL')
plt.axvline(best_bic_k, color='C0', linestyle='--', alpha=0.5)
plt.axvline(best_icl_k, color='C1', linestyle='--', alpha=0.5)
plt.xlabel('n_components (K)')
plt.ylabel('score (lower is better)')
plt.title('BIC vs ICL over K on overlapping blobs')
plt.legend()
plt.show()

print(f'BIC-optimal K = {best_bic_k}')
print(f'ICL-optimal K = {best_icl_k}')
    ks = [row['n_components'] for row in result.table] bics = [row['bic'] for row in result.table] icls = [row['icl'] for row in result.table] best_bic_k = ks[int(np.argmin(bics))] best_icl_k = ks[int(np.argmin(icls))] plt.figure(figsize=(6, 4)) plt.plot(ks, bics, marker='o', label='BIC') plt.plot(ks, icls, marker='s', label='ICL') plt.axvline(best_bic_k, color='C0', linestyle='--', alpha=0.5) plt.axvline(best_icl_k, color='C1', linestyle='--', alpha=0.5) plt.xlabel('n_components (K)') plt.ylabel('score (lower is better)') plt.title('BIC vs ICL over K on overlapping blobs') plt.legend() plt.show() print(f'BIC-optimal K = {best_bic_k}') print(f'ICL-optimal K = {best_icl_k}') 
    BIC-optimal K = 3
ICL-optimal K = 2

    As expected on this overlapping dataset, ICL settles on fewer components than BIC: BIC keeps adding components as long as they buy a bit more likelihood, while ICL's entropy penalty charges for the ambiguity introduced by splitting an overlapping pair into two components whose responsibilities are never cleanly one-hot. Neither is "wrong" -- they answer different questions (best density estimate vs. best well-separated partition).

    result.best_ is the fitted GaussianMixture that minimised the sweep's criterion ('bic' here); result.to_dataframe() gives the same table as a pandas.DataFrame for further analysis.

    icl() on a single fitted model¶

    icl(X, mode='hard') (the default) uses the most-likely component per point; mode='soft' uses the full responsibility-entropy penalty instead. Both agree exactly with bic() whenever responsibilities are one-hot (e.g. far-apart, well-separated components), and diverge more the more overlapping/ambiguous the fit is -- which is exactly what drives the gap in the curves above.

    In [6]:
    Copied! 
    gmm = result.models_[(best_bic_k, 'full')]
print('bic:      ', gmm.bic(X))
print('icl hard: ', gmm.icl(X, mode='hard'))
print('icl soft: ', gmm.icl(X, mode='soft'))
    gmm = result.models_[(best_bic_k, 'full')] print('bic: ', gmm.bic(X)) print('icl hard: ', gmm.icl(X, mode='hard')) print('icl soft: ', gmm.icl(X, mode='soft'))
